evidence.reason: The current tip confirms the gap. In `dispatch` (crq_repair.py), provider fallback admission — including the selected provider's persisted cooldown recorded by `remember_provider_limit` — is sampled before `_dispatch` runs; the wrapper's own comment states a retrying lane "must observe its provider's persisted cooldown ... instead of reopening the rate-limited lane", establishing that cooldown observance is existing intended behavior, not a new requirement. `_dispatch` then performs slow preparation (worktree retention, source-snapshot and review-diff secret scans) that the code itself says "can outlast the margin they allowed", and at the final launch boundary (lines 451-460) re-samples only the wall-clock deadline and the GLM blackout before invoking the driver at lines 461-469. No provider-cooldown recheck exists at that boundary, so a cooldown persisted concurrently by another worker during the scans is ignored and the rate-limited provider is invoked — exactly the "reopening the rate-limited lane" outcome the module's stated behavior forbids. The same staleness rationale the code already applies to deadline/blackout at this boundary covers the persisted cooldown, so this is an implementation error in existing admission behavior, not a scope enlargement or mere hardening of an advisory mechanism (nothing in the current contract retires repair-lane cooldown enforcement). The remedy is a routine, non-disruptive correctness repair: recheck the selected provider's cooldown at the same final boundary and, if active, return a local deferral the fallback loop treats as provider-unavailable without recording a new provider rate-limit response; no owner decision is needed. The finding's cited "line 321" numbering is slightly off versus the visible blob (admission sits just after `dispatch`'s start near line 329+), but the structural allegation is fully supported by the supplied region.
